question: What does the "PSLV" rocket stand for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PSLV stands for Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (ध्रुवीय उपग्रह प्रक्षेपण यान), the workhorse expendable launch vehicle of ISRO.

• It is a four-stage rocket that alternates solid and liquid propulsion stages.

• PSLV is mainly used to place remote-sensing (Earth observation) satellites into Sun-synchronous polar orbits.

• It gained global fame with the PSLV-C37 mission (2017) that launched 104 satellites in a single flight.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• PSLV also launched India's Chandrayaan-1 (2008) and Mangalyaan/Mars Orbiter Mission (2013).

• It is developed and operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).

• The first successful PSLV flight was in 1994.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): "Public Space Launch Vehicle" is not a real ISRO vehicle name.

• opt (Option 3): "Planetary Satellite Launch Vehicle" is a fabricated expansion; the P stands for Polar.

• opt (Option 4): "Private Satellite Launch Vehicle" is incorrect; PSLV is a government (ISRO) vehicle.

question: Which BIMSTEC member state leads the priority area of "Energy"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under BIMSTEC's sectoral distribution, India is the lead country for the Energy priority sector (ऊर्जा क्षेत्र).

• BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) organises cooperation into sectors, each led by a member state.

• India also leads sectors such as Transport & Communication, Tourism, Environment & Disaster Management and Counter-Terrorism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BIMSTEC has seven members: India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand.

• The BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection MoU was signed to promote energy trade among members.

• The BIMSTEC Secretariat is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Thailand leads sectors like Public Health and People-to-People Contact, not Energy.

• opt (Option 3): Sri Lanka leads Science, Technology & Innovation, not Energy.

• opt (Option 4): Bangladesh leads Trade, Investment & Development, not Energy.

question: Which government initiative aims to provide a unified platform for citizens to access various government services online?
option_2: UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance)
solution_text:
The correct answer is UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• UMANG is a single unified mobile platform (एकीकृत मोबाइल मंच) giving citizens access to a wide range of central and state government services.

• It was launched in 2017 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and NeGD.

• Through one app users can access services like EPFO, PAN, gas booking, Aadhaar, pension and utility payments.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance.

• It supports multiple Indian languages and is available on Android, iOS and web.

• It is part of the Digital India programme.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): DigiLocker is a platform for storing and sharing digital documents, not a unified services app.

• opt (Option 3): MyGov is a citizen engagement/participation platform, not a services-access app.

• opt (Option 4): NeGP is an umbrella policy framework, not a single unified citizen application.

question: Which sport is linked to the term "Grand Slam"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis, the term Grand Slam (ग्रैंड स्लैम) refers to the four most prestigious annual tournaments.

• The four Grand Slam events are the Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon and the US Open.

• Winning all four in the same calendar year is called achieving a 'Grand Slam'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament, first held in 1877, and is played on grass.

• The French Open is played on clay courts; the US and Australian Opens are on hard courts.

• The term 'Grand Slam' is also used in golf and bridge, but in the sporting exam context it is most strongly linked to tennis.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Cricket uses terms like century and hat-trick, not Grand Slam.

• opt (Option 2): Golf has 'majors'; while sometimes loosely termed a grand slam, the classic association is tennis.

• opt (Option 4): Badminton events are organised under the BWF World Tour, not called Grand Slams.

question: The inaugural edition of the Indian Women's League (IWL) football final in 2017 was hosted in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The inaugural Indian Women's League (IWL) final in 2017 was hosted in New Delhi (नई दिल्ली).

• The IWL is the top-tier women's football league in India, organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

• Eastern Sporting Union won the first IWL title in 2017.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first edition matches were played at the Ambedkar Stadium in New Delhi.

• The IWL was created to strengthen the base of women's football in India.

• Rani Kumari and Bala Devi were among the notable performers in the early editions.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): Shillong is a football hub but did not host the inaugural IWL final.

• opt (Option 3): Kolkata is historically important for Indian football but not the 2017 IWL final venue.

• opt (Option 4): Mumbai did not host the inaugural IWL final.

question: The festival of "Phool Dei" is unique to which of the following Indian regions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumaon Hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Phool Dei is a folk festival unique to the Kumaon (and Garhwal) hills (कुमाऊँ की पहाड़ियाँ) of Uttarakhand.

• It is a spring/harvest festival celebrated at the start of the Hindu month of Chaitra.

• Young girls decorate the thresholds of homes with flowers, jaggery and rice, seeking prosperity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The dish 'Dei' (a sweet pudding of jaggery and curd) gives the festival part of its name.

• It reflects the deep connection of Uttarakhand's culture with nature and the changing seasons.

• The festival is also known as Phul Dei / Phool Sankranti.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The Deccan Plateau is in peninsular India and unrelated to Phool Dei.

• opt (Option 2): The Malwa Plateau lies mainly in Madhya Pradesh, not the region of Phool Dei.

• opt (Option 4): The Western Ghats run along the west coast and are unrelated to this Uttarakhand festival.

question: Which of the following changes has been introduced to ensure faster trials under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Video recording of statements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 introduced video/audio-visual recording of statements (बयानों की वीडियो रिकॉर्डिंग) to speed up and strengthen trials.

• BNSS replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, from 1 July 2024.

• It promotes the use of technology, e-records, and digital evidence to reduce delays.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BNSS mandates timelines, such as delivering judgment within 45 days of completion of trial in certain cases.

• It provides for trial in absentia of proclaimed offenders and use of electronic communication for proceedings.

• Search and seizure operations are to be audio-video recorded, preferably by mobile phone.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): A ban on legal representation would violate the right to counsel; BNSS does not do this.

• opt (Option 3): Removal of judges is unrelated and not a feature of BNSS.

• opt (Option 4): Delay in filing chargesheets would slow trials, the opposite of the Act's aim.

question: Who was appointed as the Union Law Secretary in March 2025, becoming the first woman to hold this position?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anju Rathi Rana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anju Rathi Rana (अंजू राठी राणा) became the first woman to be appointed Union Law Secretary in March 2025.

• She belongs to the Indian Legal Service and heads the Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice.

• Her appointment marked a historic milestone for gender representation in top legal administrative posts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Law Secretary is the administrative head of the Department of Legal Affairs.

• The Ministry of Law and Justice comprises the Departments of Legal Affairs, Legislative, and Justice.

• The appointment is made by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC).

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Shelly Oberoi was Mayor of Delhi, not the Union Law Secretary.

• opt (Option 2): Atishi Marlena is a politician and former Delhi Chief Minister, not the Law Secretary.

• opt (Option 4): Rekha Gupta is a Delhi politician, not the Union Law Secretary.

question: Why does the Tamil Nadu coast remain dry during the southwest monsoon?
option_1: Due to the presence of extra-tropical cyclonic situations during the winters.
option_2: It receives most of the rainfall from tropical cyclones originating over the Arabian Sea.
option_3: It is situated parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon.
option_4: The inter-tropical convergence zone is located below the Tropic of Capricorn during the winter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is situated parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tamil Nadu (Coromandel) coast lies parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch (बंगाल की खाड़ी शाखा के समानांतर) of the southwest monsoon, so the winds blow along the coast instead of striking it.

• Because the moisture-bearing winds run parallel rather than perpendicular, they do not shed rain here.

• It also lies in the rain-shadow of the Arabian Sea branch, which is blocked by the Western Ghats.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall during the northeast (retreating) monsoon in October to December.

• The Coromandel Coast is therefore one of the few Indian regions that is wet in the winter monsoon season.

• The Western Ghats create heavy orographic rain on the windward (western) side, leaving the eastern side drier.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Extra-tropical cyclones in winter are not the reason the coast is dry in the southwest monsoon.

• opt (Option 2): Tamil Nadu gets rain mainly from the northeast monsoon over the Bay of Bengal, not Arabian Sea cyclones.

• opt (Option 4): The ITCZ position statement does not explain the southwest-monsoon dryness of the coast.

question: Which foreign element, stemming from Achaemenid Persia, influenced Mauryan sculpture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bold and massive realism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mauryan sculpture, influenced by Achaemenid Persia, is marked by bold and massive realism (साहसिक एवं व्यापक यथार्थवाद) with a high lustrous polish.

• The famous Mauryan polished stone pillars and animal capitals reflect this Persian-inspired monumental style.

• The Lion Capital of Sarnath is the finest example of this bold, realistic and polished tradition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The characteristic 'Mauryan polish' on sandstone is a hallmark of this period.

• The bell-shaped (Persepolitan) capitals of Ashokan pillars show direct Achaemenid influence.

• The Lion Capital of Sarnath is India's national emblem.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Terracotta was widely used in India before the Mauryas and is not the Persian-derived element in stone sculpture.

• opt (Option 3): Employment of specific deities is not the Achaemenid contribution to Mauryan sculpture.

• opt (Option 4): Intricate filigree work is a metalworking technique, not the feature borrowed here.

question: Which title used by Gupta rulers reflected their Vaishnavite affiliation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paramabhagavata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gupta rulers adopted the title Paramabhagavata (परमभागवत) to reflect their devotion to Vishnu (Vaishnavism).

• 'Bhagavata' denotes a devotee of Bhagavan (Vishnu), so 'Paramabhagavata' means 'supreme devotee of Vishnu'.

• Many Gupta kings, such as Chandragupta II and Skandagupta, were staunch Vaishnavites.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Gupta period is often called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India.

• The Garuda (mount of Vishnu) featured on Gupta coins and seals, underlining their Vaishnavite leanings.

• Chandragupta II bore the title Vikramaditya.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Lokadhama-deva is not the standard Vaishnavite title of the Guptas.

• opt (Option 2): Parameshvara is a Shaivite-flavoured/imperial title meaning supreme lord, not specifically Vaishnavite.

• opt (Option 4): Paramatman is a philosophical term for the Supreme Soul, not an imperial title of affiliation.

question:
Arrange the following historical events in their correct chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
1. Construction of the Grand Trunk Road
2. Akbar begins his reign
3. Death of Humayun
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-3-2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Grand Trunk Road (ग्रैंड ट्रंक रोड) was rebuilt by Sher Shah Suri around 1540 to 1545, the earliest event.

• Humayun died in early 1556 after a fall from his library stairs.

• Akbar then ascended the throne (began his reign) in February 1556.

• Hence the order earliest to latest is: Grand Trunk Road (1) then Death of Humayun (3) then Akbar's reign (2).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sher Shah Suri's road ran from Bengal to the northwest and was later called the Grand Trunk Road.

• Akbar was only 13 when he was crowned; Bairam Khan served as his regent.

• Akbar reigned from 1556 to 1605.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 3-2-1 wrongly places the Grand Trunk Road last.

• opt (Option 3): 2-1-3 wrongly starts with Akbar's reign before the road's construction.

• opt (Option 4): 1-2-3 wrongly places Akbar's reign before Humayun's death.

question: The Governor General's Council, as established by the Regulating Act, consisted of how many members?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act of 1773 created a Governor-General of Bengal assisted by a Council of four members (चार सदस्य).

• Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal under this Act.

• Decisions in the council were taken by majority vote.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS (continued)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Regulating Act was the first step by the British Parliament to control the East India Company's affairs.

• It also established a Supreme Court at Calcutta (Fort William) in 1774.

• The Pitt's India Act of 1784 later reduced the council and set up a Board of Control.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Three is incorrect; the council had four members under the Act.

• opt (Option 3): Five does not match the composition fixed by the Regulating Act.

• opt (Option 4): Six is incorrect for the Regulating Act council.

question:
Fill in the blanks:
The Summer Olympics held in _________ in August 2004 featured India's first Olympic shooting medal won by Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Athens, Greece.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2004 Summer Olympics were held in Athens, Greece (एथेंस, ग्रीस).

• Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won a silver medal in men's double trap shooting, India's first Olympic shooting medal.

• It was India's only medal at the Athens 2004 Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Athens 2004 marked the return of the modern Olympics to their birthplace (Greece).

• Abhinav Bindra later won India's first individual Olympic gold, also in shooting, at Beijing 2008.

• Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore later became a Union Minister.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Beijing, China hosted the 2008 Olympics, not 2004.

• opt (Option 2): Sydney, Australia hosted the 2000 Olympics.

• opt (Option 4): Atlanta, USA hosted the 1996 Olympics.

question: What is the central theme of the book 'Friend of My Youth' by Amit Chaudhuri?
option_1: A collection of interconnected stories exploring Indian family and identity
option_2: A historical account of India's independence struggle
option_3: A travelogue about India's diverse landscapes
option_4: A biography of a famous Indian politician
solution_text:
The correct answer is A collection of interconnected stories exploring Indian family and identity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Friend of My Youth' by Amit Chaudhuri is a reflective, semi-autobiographical work exploring memory, family and identity (परिवार और पहचान).

• Set largely in Mumbai (Bombay), it follows a narrator, also named Amit, returning to his childhood city.

• It weaves together personal recollection, friendship and a meditation on the city and the self.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Amit Chaudhuri is an acclaimed Indian novelist, essayist and musician.

• His notable works include 'A Strange and Sublime Address' and 'A New World'.

• He has won the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Commonwealth Writers' Prize.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): The book is not a historical account of the independence struggle.

• opt (Option 3): It is not primarily a travelogue about India's landscapes.

• opt (Option 4): It is not a biography of a politician.

question:
Fill in the blanks:
Even after a Bill is passed by the State Legislature, the Governor may forward it to the _______ for consideration.
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 200 of the Constitution, a Governor may reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President (राष्ट्रपति).

• When so reserved, the Bill does not become law until the President assents to it (Article 201).

• The President may assent, withhold assent, or direct the Governor to return the Bill (if not a Money Bill) for reconsideration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Bill that endangers the position of the High Court is compulsorily reserved for the President.

• The Governor's options on a Bill are: assent, withhold assent, return, or reserve for the President.

• The President is not bound by any time limit under Article 201 to act on a reserved Bill.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The Chief Minister is the head of the state government but does not receive Bills for constitutional assent.

• opt (Option 2): The Speaker presides over the Assembly but is not the authority for reserving Bills.

• opt (Option 4): The Prime Minister heads the Union executive and has no role in state Bill assent.

question: What happens during beta-plus (β+) decay in a nucleus?
option_1: Proton number decreases by 1, mass number remains unchanged
option_2: Proton number increases by 1, mass number remains unchanged
option_3: Both proton number and mass number decrease
option_4: Proton number decreases by 2, mass number decreases by 4
solution_text:
The correct answer is Proton number decreases by 1, mass number remains unchanged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In beta-plus (β+) decay (बीटा-प्लस क्षय), a proton converts into a neutron, emitting a positron and a neutrino.

• The atomic (proton) number decreases by 1, while the mass number stays the same.

• The daughter nucleus therefore shifts one place to the left in the periodic table.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The reaction can be written as p to n + e+ + neutrino.

• In beta-minus (β-) decay, a neutron becomes a proton, so the proton number increases by 1.

• Alpha decay reduces the mass number by 4 and the proton number by 2.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): An increase in proton number describes beta-minus (β-) decay, not β+.

• opt (Option 3): Both numbers decreasing does not correctly describe β+ decay.

• opt (Option 4): A decrease of 2 in proton number and 4 in mass number describes alpha decay.

question: According to the World Economic Forum's 2025 Energy Transition Index (ETI), which trend best reflects the current state of global energy systems?
option_2: Demand up due to electrification and cooling
solution_text:
The correct answer is Demand up due to electrification and cooling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The WEF 2025 Energy Transition Index notes that global energy demand is rising due to electrification and cooling (विद्युतीकरण और शीतलन के कारण मांग बढ़ी).

• Growing electrification of transport and industry, plus higher cooling needs, are pushing demand upward.

• The ETI benchmarks countries on the performance and readiness of their energy systems.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The ETI evaluates energy systems on security, sustainability and equity, plus transition readiness.

• Rising cooling demand is closely linked to warming temperatures and rising incomes.

• The report is published annually by the World Economic Forum.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): 'Security up, sustainability down' is not the highlighted trend in the 2025 ETI framing.

• opt (Option 3): AI cutting demand and stabilising the grid is not the reported trend.

• opt (Option 4): A blanket 'investment and readiness above average' does not capture the demand-growth trend.

question:
Consider the statements about Ghoomar :
1. Its earliest performers were Bhil women; Rajputs later adopted it.
2. Ghoomar was inscribed on UNESCO ICH list in 2015.
Which is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct: Ghoomar (घूमर) was originally performed by Bhil women and was later adopted by the Rajputs of Rajasthan.

• Statement 2 is incorrect: Ghoomar has NOT been inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

• Ghoomar is a graceful whirling folk dance traditionally performed by women in flowing ghagra dresses.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ghoomar is associated with the Rajput community and festive/ceremonial occasions in Rajasthan.

• Indian traditions on the UNESCO ICH list include Kutiyattam, Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja and Garba of Gujarat.

• The dance takes its name from 'ghoomna', the pirouetting (twirling) movement.

NOTE

• opt (Option 2): 'Only 2 correct' is wrong because statement 2 (UNESCO 2015 inscription) is false.

• opt (Option 3): 'Both 1 & 2 correct' is wrong since statement 2 is false.

• opt (Option 4): 'Neither correct' is wrong since statement 1 is true.

question: Which of the following is an example of a capital receipt?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loan taken from RBI.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A loan taken from the RBI is a capital receipt (पूंजी प्राप्ति) because it creates a liability (it must be repaid).

• Capital receipts either create a liability (borrowings) or reduce an asset (disinvestment).

• Revenue receipts, by contrast, neither create a liability nor reduce assets.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Examples of capital receipts: borrowings, recovery of loans, and disinvestment proceeds.

• Examples of revenue receipts: taxes, interest, dividends, fees and fines.

• The distinction is central to the structure of the Union Budget.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Income tax collected is a revenue receipt, not a capital receipt.

• opt (Option 2): Dividend from PSUs is a non-tax revenue receipt.

• opt (Option 4): Sale proceeds of public services are revenue receipts.

question: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, also known as 'Kappalottiya Thamizhan', was a pioneer of the Swadeshi movement who started which enterprise?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company (स्वदेशी स्टीम नेविगेशन कंपनी) in 1906.

• He earned the title 'Kappalottiya Thamizhan' (the Tamil who steered the ship) for this venture.

• The company ran ships between Tuticorin and Colombo, challenging British shipping monopoly.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• V.O.C. was a close associate of Bal Gangadhar Tilak and a leader of the extremist wing of the Congress.

• He was imprisoned and sentenced to rigorous punishment, including being made to pull an oil press in jail.

• He was a lawyer, freedom fighter and trade unionist from Tamil Nadu.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): He did not found a 'Swadeshi Cotton Mills' as his signature enterprise.

• opt (Option 3): 'Swadeshi Bank' was not his enterprise.

• opt (Option 4): 'Swadeshi Textile Mills' was not the company he started.

question: How does Indian planning demonstrate responsiveness to feedback?
option_1: By finalizing plans before public opinion is known
option_3: By modifying drafts based on criticism and recommendations
option_4: By consulting only foreign agencies for planning
solution_text:
The correct answer is By modifying drafts based on criticism and recommendations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian planning shows responsiveness by modifying draft plans based on criticism and recommendations (आलोचना और सिफारिशों के आधार पर).

• Draft plans were circulated for discussion, and feedback from experts, states and the public shaped the final plan.

• This consultative, iterative process reflects the democratic nature of Indian planning.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Planning Commission (1950 to 2014) prepared the Five-Year Plans through such consultation.

• The NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, emphasising cooperative federalism.

• Plans were finally approved by the National Development Council.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Finalizing plans before public opinion is known shows the opposite of responsiveness.

• opt (Option 2): Discarding public suggestions entirely is not responsive to feedback.

• opt (Option 4): Consulting only foreign agencies ignores domestic feedback.

question: Which of the following statements about Verghese Kurien is correct?
option_1: He initiated the White Revolution in India's IT sector.
option_2: He pioneered Operation Flood to transform dairy farming.
option_3: He invented the milk pasteurization method used in Amul.
option_4: He was the first Chairman of the Indian Dairy Association.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He pioneered Operation Flood to transform dairy farming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Verghese Kurien pioneered Operation Flood (ऑपरेशन फ्लड), the world's largest dairy development programme.

• Known as the 'Father of the White Revolution', he made India the world's largest milk producer.

• He founded the Amul cooperative model at Anand, Gujarat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).

• Kurien was the founder-chairman of the NDDB and the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (Amul).

• He received the Padma Vibhushan and the World Food Prize.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): The White Revolution relates to milk/dairy, not the IT sector.

• opt (Option 3): He did not invent milk pasteurization; his contribution was the cooperative and Operation Flood.

• opt (Option 4): He was chairman of the NDDB and GCMMF, not described as first chairman of an 'Indian Dairy Association'.

question: Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect is primarily caused by which of the following urban factors?
option_3: Concrete structures, low vegetation, and vehicular heat
option_4: High-altitude rural zones and river valleys
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concrete structures, low vegetation, and vehicular heat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Urban Heat Island effect is mainly caused by concrete structures, low vegetation and vehicular/anthropogenic heat (कंक्रीट संरचनाएं, कम वनस्पति और वाहनों की गर्मी).

• Concrete and asphalt absorb and re-radiate heat, keeping cities warmer than surrounding rural areas.

• Reduced greenery lowers cooling from evapotranspiration, while traffic and industry add waste heat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• UHI intensity is usually strongest at night when built surfaces release stored heat.

• Remedies include urban green spaces, cool/reflective roofs and increased tree cover.

• Dark low-albedo surfaces worsen the effect by absorbing more solar radiation.

NOTE

• opt (Option 1): Increased humidity in peri-urban regions is not the primary cause of UHI.

• opt (Option 2): Dense vegetation and water bodies actually reduce heat, not cause UHI.

• opt (Option 4): High-altitude rural zones and river valleys are not urban heat-island drivers.

question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 246A grants exclusive power to Parliament to make laws on GST.
2. States have no legislative power over intra-state GST.
3. GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 3 is correct: the GST Council (जीएसटी परिषद) is a constitutional body established under Article 279A.

• Statement 1 is wrong: Article 246A gives concurrent power to both Parliament and State Legislatures on GST, not exclusive power to Parliament (Parliament has exclusive power only over inter-state supply/IGST).

• Statement 2 is wrong: States do have legislative power over intra-state GST (SGST).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 246A and the GST framework were introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.

• The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with state finance ministers as members.

• GST is a destination-based, multi-stage tax with input tax credit.

NOTE
